topics.title: What the course covers
topics.intro: The course covers the IBLCE content areas, including anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pathology and clinical skills. It also addresses breastfeeding beliefs and practices in Asian cultures, from the effect of traditional confinement diets on milk supply to family dynamics around breastfeeding decisions.

items.oral: Infant oral anatomy and suckling mechanics
items.management: Breastfeeding management across the first year
items.challenges: Low supply, engorgement, mastitis and tongue-tie
items.special: Preterm infants, multiples and the NICU

what.a: The International Board Certified Lactation Consultant (IBCLC) is a credential for lactation care professionals, issued by the International Board of Lactation Consultant Examiners (IBLCE). It requires specialized education, clinical experience and a pass on IBLCE’s exam.

issue.q: Does ADA issue the IBCLC credential?
issue.a: No. The IBCLC is issued by IBLCE. ADA provides the exam-prep course that covers the lactation-specific education hours required to sit the IBCLC exam, and records your completion.

adaFirst.q: Do I need to be an ADA-certified doula first?
adaFirst.a: No. The course is open to anyone who meets IBLCE’s eligibility requirements, including nurses, midwives and other health professionals.

next.a: Cohorts run on a rolling basis throughout the year. Write to us to join the next cohort’s roster. We will share start dates, pricing and, if you need them, referrals to partner IBCLC training organizations for clinical hours.

cost.a: Write to <mail>{email}</mail> for current cohort pricing, payment plan options and referrals to partner programs for any clinical hours ADA does not provide.
